name: NetExec - Password Spraying
description: Password spraying tries one password against many accounts to stay under lockout thresholds, optionally across a whole subnet. Reverse of brute forcing (many passwords, one account). Ideal with a single common password.

examples.label: Spray one password across a subnet

notes:
Password spraying: ONE password against MANY users to dodge lockout (`nxc smb <dc> -u users.txt -p 'Season2024!'`). Exclude accounts near badPwdCount. The safest way to turn a name list into valid creds.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

defense.why_it_works: Password spraying tries ONE common password across MANY accounts to avoid lockouts while still catching weak passwords.
defense.prerequisites: A user list and one/few candidate passwords; access to the auth service.
defense.impact: Compromised accounts using the sprayed password - often a domain foothold.
defense.detection: Failed authentication bursts: Windows 4625 (failed logon) and 4771 (Kerberos pre-auth failed) at abnormal rate/volume; account lockouts (4740); many attempts from one source, or - for spraying - one password across many accounts. SIEM correlation on failed-logon spikes.
defense.artifacts: One password attempted against many accounts (few failures per account); subtle 4625 pattern, minimal lockouts.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1110 M1032 Multi-factor Authentication] MFA defeats password guessing; [M1027 Password Policies] strong passwords + [M1036 Account Use Policies] lockout thresholds; alert on failed-logon spikes and impossible-travel.
defense.evasion: Spray low-and-slow (one password, spaced attempts) to stay under lockout thresholds and volume alerts; distribute across source IPs; target accounts unlikely to be monitored.
defense.misconfiguration: The domain's lockout policy is either disabled or set with a threshold high enough (e.g., 10 attempts before lockout) that a low-and-slow spray — one guess per account per 30 minutes — never triggers lockout. Additionally, many accounts share the same simple passwords (company name + year, Season+Year), and the bad-password counter resets after the observation window elapses.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Weak lockout policy (domain default or intentionally lenient):
# Fine-Grained Password Policy:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# LockoutObservationWindow: 00:30:00
# LockoutThreshold:         0          <-- DISABLED! No lockout ever
# OR: LockoutThreshold: 10 (attacker sprays 9 per window, never locks)

# Also: accounts with password = company name:
# Common passwords: Summer2023!, Winter2024!, CompanyName1!
defense.secure_config:
# Set a strong lockout policy:
# Via Default Domain Policy or Fine-Grained Password Policy (PSO):
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local \
    -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutThreshold 5
# LockoutThreshold 5 means 5 bad attempts in 30 min = 30-min lockout

# Fine-Grained PSO for admins (stricter):
New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name AdminPSO \
    -LockoutThreshold 3 -LockoutDuration 01:00:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 01:00:00 \
    -Precedence 1
Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject AdminPSO -Subjects 'Domain Admins'

# Enable Azure AD / Entra ID Password Protection (bans common passwords):
# Also available on-premises via the Azure AD Password Protection agent

# Monitor Event 4740 (Account Locked Out) — spray leaves a cluster of these
